newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dutch target Australia's TNT in A$2 bln takeover.
newsitem.headline: Dutch target Australia's TNT in A$2 bln takeover.

text.p: Worldwide Australian transport group TNT Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to a A$2 billion (US$1.58 billion) takeover offer from Dutch Telecom and Postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) NV.

"The directors of TNT unanimously recommend that shareholders in TNT accept KPN's offer, in the absence of a superior offer, as they intend to do in respect of all of their own shares and share options," TNT and KPN said in a joint statement.
"It will create a new global force in the time-sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four world-wide," the companies said.
The A$2.45 per share cash takeover offer values TNT at A$2 billion, a 48 percent premium to its current market capitalisation.
KPN is the primary postal and telecommunications corporation of the Netherlands and TNT transport and logistics group is based in Australia.
The takeover agreement followed long, strategic discussions between KPN and TNT about the benefits of combining TNT's businesses with KPN's postal subsidiary, the statement said.

Last month, TNT reported another annual profit slump, but promised the sale of 50 percent stake in the troubled Australian carrier Ansett Airlines and other reforms would produce strong profit growth in the current year.
TNT's net profit for the year to June 30 fell to A$9.84 million from A$40.01 million in 1994/95 and A$105.05 million in 1993/94.
TNT's share price closed up two cents at A$1.63 on Tuesday.
